# Source 104 — Jamestown: Xi Pursues AI Governance Leadership at Beijing Summit

- **URL:** https://jamestown.org/xi-pursues-ai-governance-leadership-at-beijing-summit/
- **Authors:** Sunny Cheung, Shijie Wang (Jamestown Foundation)
- **Published:** 2026-07-22
- **Type:** Policy analysis (think-tank)
- **Status:** fetched 2026-09-14 (full text, http 200)

## Key claims (as stated in source)
- On July 17, 2026 Xi Jinping addressed the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference and High-Level Meeting on AI Global Governance in Shanghai; his keynote centered on "when machines begin thinking, how will humans coexist with them?"
- The **World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO; 世界人工智能合作组织)** was unveiled at the conference, to be headquartered in Shanghai, and is "billed as the first intergovernmental body dedicated to AI" (attributed to Xinhua, July 17).
- Xi framed WAICO as aimed at closing the "intelligence gap" (智能鸿沟) for developing states.
- Pledged: 5,000 AI "research and training opportunities" (研修培训名额) via centers in ASEAN, the Arab League, the African Union, SCO, Latin America, and BRICS; and the **Mazu (妈祖) meteorological AI system to 30 countries**.
- The NDRC released an eight-point "Action Plan" (July 17) described as a blueprint for underwriting global AI governance (R&D cooperation, shared data/compute, embedding PRC norms into international rules).
- Xi endorsed embedding AI in physical robotics; the expo showcased dexterous robotic hands and brain-to-robot control platforms.
- Countries including **Cambodia, Thailand, and Kazakhstan** endorsed Beijing's regulatory approach following the conference (attributed to MFA, July 17; People's Daily, July 19).
- Footnote: WAICO follows the World Data Organization unveiled by Beijing in May 2026.
- Footnote: 2026 domestic AI regulations include the "Interim Measures on AI Anthropomorphic Interactive Services" (issued April 10 by CAC and other regulators) — bans virtual companions for minors, mandates distress detection, security assessment filings; plus April draft rules on digital virtual humans and public penalties against ByteDance-affiliated apps for failing to label AI-generated content.

## Verification notes
- Consistent with draft.md usage (WAICO unveiling, 5,000 training, Mazu to 30 countries, Global South targeting).
- Think-tank analysis; factual claims attributed to Xinhua/MFA/NDRC/People's Daily. Interpretive framing (strategy assessment) is the authors'.
- Note: article title says "Beijing Summit" but the event described is WAIC in Shanghai.
